text.p: On overnight commodity markets, copper prices firmed in London on short covering, edging back towards the US$2,000 mark.

Wheat prices also closed higher on short covering while oil prices firmed on news of production cuts linked to a storm. Gold prices rose, partly on news fund managers overall held net short positions.
Sugar prices fell in thin dealings. The CRB index closed up 1.33 points at 249.14.

Flurries of short covering following gains in New York boosted London Metal Exchange (LME) copper prices by the close of Tuesday's business. Traders aid it was a move that looked set to continue as trade confidence returned following recent long liquidation. Benchmark three months delivery copper ended at $1,949, $5 below its high but well up on Monday's $1,905. "Chartwise the late rally has left copper open to further gains toward $2,000," one LME floor trader said. Fundamentals have improved recently, a condition backed up by falling LME inventories, which are expected to continue to decline over the coming weeks. Earlier LME stocks fell by 8,625 tonnes. Other
metals remained quiet but followed copper higher. Oversold conditions bolster aluminium which was last at $1,346.50, versus $1,336. Nickel, despite a stocks rise, jumped to $7,160, against $7,030.

CBOT wheat futures closed higher on short covering amid very thin volume, traders said. "It's a little technical short covering. There are too many shorts going into the report Friday, a little nervousness around," said Skip Searcy, wheat trading specialist for FIMAT Futures. USDA at 0730 CDT Friday
will release its October crop production and supply/demand reports. Wheat futures closed 2-1/2 to six cents per bushel higher, with December up six at $4.28-1/2.

NYMEX crude prices ended higher Tuesday on news that Tropical Storm Josephine cut output in some fields and closed ports in the Gulf of Mexico. "The port situation had to have lent support since it will tighten supplies," said a trader in Texas. November crude ended 30 cents higher at $25.54 a barrel. Crude hit a session high of $25.60, 10 cents shy of the

post-Gulf War high hit last April. Traders estimated 600,000 barrels were lost in crude output after Josephine swept through the Gulf of Mexico over the weekend. Josephine disrupted shipping at the deepwater Louisiana Offshore Oil Port and closed two major Mexican terminals, Pajaritos and Dos Bocas.

New York precious metals futures ended mostly higher Tuesday, as the complex continued to attempt a recovery from a month-long downtrend. "It's been a plodding recovery though in the past week, hardly a heroic effort," Chase Manhattan New York

based managing director Dinsa Mehta said. "The selling has been absorbed, gold equity funds have been adding bullion to their portfolios, and fabricator demand has picked up, but the big fund shorts are still in market, and the recovery is likely to remain mild unless large scale fund shortcovering occurs," he said. The most recent CFTC Commitment of Traders data showed funds with record net short positions, analysts noted. COMEX December gold ended up 80 cents at $383.40 an ounce, after trading in a $382.60-384.30 range. CSCE world sugar futures limped lower in thin dealings, while prices remained stuck in their recent trading range. A dearth of news and the nearly four months remaining before the March contract expires is likely to keep pressure off the market, dealers said. Volume was estimated at only 7,447 lots. March closed 0.06 lower at 10.82, having ranged from 10.87 to 10.77. The back months settled 0.01 lower to 0.03 firmer. Support remained in the mid 10.70-cent per lb range and
resistance in the mid 10.90s, dealers said.
